replayComponent.scope: complete-installer package only; no other component payload changed in this cycle.
replayComponent.change: New -ReplayComponent <component-id> parameter on Invoke-KIStackCompleteInstaller.ps1 and Start-KIStackCompleteInstaller.ps1, threaded through New-KICompletePlan. A component listed there and already compliant is planned with plannedMode='Replay' instead of 'Skip' and re-runs its existing install/validate/backup path unchanged; only openwebui-visual-pack and openwebui-agent-pack are permitted. An unknown or non-permitted component id throws before any plan step is built, i.e. before any mutation. New-KICompletePlan's alreadyCompliant field keeps its original, honest meaning (raw compliance); a new hasReplay field is combined with it to gate Invoke-KIStackCompleteInstaller's already-compliant short-circuit so a requested replay is never silently skipped. No existing compliance check, and no Upgrade/Repair/Skip dispatch for any other component, was changed; no file is deleted and no pinned component version is changed to manufacture artificial non-compliance; replaying one component never cascades to a dependent one.
replayComponent.validation: Test-KIStackReplayComponent.ps1: compliant+no-replay stays Skip, compliant+replay resolves to Replay without affecting sibling components (no implicit recursion), unknown component id throws, known-but-not-permitted component id throws, a genuinely non-compliant component's normal Upgrade path is unaffected, the early-return guard is statically confirmed wired to hasReplay, and the guided OpenWebUI cutover is demonstrably entered when a step arrives with plannedMode='Replay' -- all PASS. Full existing regression suite unaffected.

updateKIStackAll.scope: complete-installer package only; no other component payload changed in this cycle.
updateKIStackAll.change: New Lifecycle/Update-KIStack-All.cmd + .ps1, deployed to C:\KI-Stack, enumerates every Contracts/COMPONENTS.json component plus OpenWebUI (tracked separately) and reports InstalledVersion, PinnedVersion, AvailableVersion and a classification (UpToDate/PinnedUpdatePending/DowngradeRequired/Blocked/NotManaged) that compares only InstalledVersion against PinnedVersion and is the sole basis for automatic execution. A separate upstreamStatus (Current/UpdateAvailableUpstream/Unknown), from real read-only PyPI/GitHub lookups where a reliable upstream source exists, is purely informational and never triggers an unattended install; AvailableVersion=Unknown is the honest result for components with no such source rather than a guess. OpenWebUI executes through its own already-validated isolated adapter (Update-KIStack-OpenWebUI.cmd); every other component runs through the existing Complete-Installer-Upgrade batch, and an explicit -Component selection that would understate that batch's real scope is refused before any confirmation prompt or mutation. Also fixes Remove-KIStackKnowledgeExperiment.ps1, whose Knowledge-rollback readback validation previously only set passed:false without throwing, silently allowing a genuine validation failure to be recorded as success; it now throws on that condition, matching the sibling Code-Interpreter step's existing pattern.
updateKIStackAll.validation: Test-KIStackUpdateAll.ps1 (14/14): all components already at pin -> only UpToDate; one component behind its pin -> PinnedUpdatePending; installed above the pin -> DowngradeRequired; an unmanaged requested component id -> NotManaged; upstream UpdateAvailableUpstream on an already-compliant component is reported but never auto-executed (both CheckOnly and full-run NoActionNeeded checked); sequential execution (OpenWebUI first, then the batch); a failing OpenWebUI adapter stops before the batch ever runs and its rollback detail is surfaced, not discarded; a non-EXECUTE confirmation cancels before anything runs; a partial -Component selection against a multi-component batch is blocked before mutation, naming every attached component still proceeds, and -Component openwebui alone is unaffected by an unrelated batch ambiguity; no secret handling introduced; the normal installer's ReplayComponent/Upgrade dispatch and starter registration are unaffected -- all PASS.

codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.rootCause: Ensure-KILMStudioEndpointReachable's own retry budget (30 attempts * 2s = 60s) was independently timed and shorter than the managed LM Studio starter's genuine first-run contract (up to ~120s: 90s for the lms CLI to appear after LM Studio's first GUI launch, plus 30s for the server it starts to accept connections), and the starter's own process/exit code was never observed -- reproduced live during the 2.5.0 Greenfield acceptance run (Codex Local failed with 'LM Studio /v1/models ist nicht erreichbar' while the starter's first-run GUI wait was still legitimately in progress).
codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.fix: The starter is now treated as the authoritative start/timeout contract rather than a second, independently-timed one: the default retry budget is sized to the starter's own up-to-120s window, and the starter's own process handle is tracked so a real starter failure (non-zero exit) is detected and surfaced immediately via a new starterExitCode field instead of being silently outlived by continued polling for the rest of the budget.
codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.scope: codex-local module only; no changes to the LM Studio starter itself (KIModuleApplications.psm1) or to any other component.
codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.validation: Test-KIStackCodexLocal.ps1: a static, zero-sleep assertion on the shipped default values (total budget >= 120s) plus fast behavioral checks that a starter's own exit code is observed immediately and that a genuine timeout still fails. Negative control confirmed: reverting the fix reproduces exactly this failure.

findings.description: Receive-Artifact issued a Range request starting at the already-complete artifact's end-of-file offset (Range: bytes=<ExpectedSize>-) whenever a fully-downloaded .partial file had not yet been moved to its final target, and the source correctly answered HTTP 416 Range Not Satisfiable. Fixed: a .partial file already at the exact expected size is now verified directly via the existing size/SHA256 contract, issuing no HTTP request; a hash mismatch fails safely through the existing invalid-artifact contract, never a silent reuse.

researchAgentWebSearchValidation.rootCause: Level B, precisely isolated: native function-calling tool injection (search_web/fetch_url) in the real, installed OpenWebUI 0.11.1 source is gated on a non-empty metadata.session_id (utils/middleware.py's use_builtin_tools) -- a plain Bearer-token API call without one never receives the tool at all. With session_id present, tool injection and the model's own tool-calling behavior are both correct. OpenWebUI's own further automatic background-task execution/continuation of that tool call (used when session_id and a real chat_id are both present) has a separate, real, reproducible stall after the initial knowledge_search preprocessing step, independent of Redis/SearXNG availability -- an OpenWebUI-core limitation for non-browser callers, not an Agent Pack or model defect, and out of scope to patch from this repository.
researchAgentWebSearchValidation.change: No Agent Pack code change was required -- ki-stack-research's own provisioned fields (capabilities.web_search, builtinTools.web_search, params.function_calling=native, real Knowledge binding) were already correct, confirmed by reading the live OpenWebUI object back directly.

wslKeeperArchitectureReview.outcome: notABug -- existing architecture confirmed sound: Start-KIStack-SearXNG.ps1's keeper is already de-duplication-safe (a recorded PID is re-verified as a genuine matching wsl.exe process, via Test-KeeperIdentity, before a new keeper is ever started), Stop-KIStack-SearXNG.ps1 deliberately terminates it, and no automatic restart after reboot is intended (KI-Stack is deliberately service-free/manual-start by design). Observed instability during this session's own automated testing is attributed to this sandboxed session's own process-lifecycle handling of detached background processes, not a defect in the real script for a real interactive user. No Windows service introduced; no code change made.
